clue.text: A treasonous emu I, wandering in to seduce beauty in aria

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in between the L and the URE of the word for tempting

parts.note: to lure is to seduce

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: a belle is a beauty

explanation.surface: A traitorous emu (and the speaker) wanders into some seduction during a pretty aria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' makes AMOURESTUNOISEA; the lure is split open by it, its L kept apart. The line opens Carmen's Habanera: 'Love is a rebellious bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Habanera from Bizet's Carmen, which opens with this line, is a famous operatic aria.

clue.text: Beast saying prayer?

indicators.note: saying means the word is spoken, so we want something sounding the same

parts.note: a lama, a Tibetan Buddhist monk, is one who prays

explanation.surface: A cryptic question: which animal is saying its prayers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'prayer' is read as one who prays, a Buddhist monk.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American pack animal, a beast of burden.

clue.text: Seafood, a smaller quantity in total that's hauled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, hauling something up reads it from bottom to top, so backwards
the smaller quantity sits inside the word for total

parts.note: a sum is a total
less means a smaller quantity

explanation.surface: Seafood brought up by a net, with a smaller haul in all.
explanation.walkthrough: LESS goes 'in' SUM to give SLESSUM, which 'hauled up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussels are shellfish eaten as seafood, an example of the category.

clue.text: Top broadcaster, free

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Auntie is the affectionate nickname of the BBC

explanation.surface: A leading broadcaster offers something free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie' (or 'Auntie Beeb') is a British nickname for the BBC; 'Top' removes its first letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something knotted is to unfasten it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: See 6
Terrible start and horrid end in an earlier clue made less shocking

indicators.note: the start of the word Terrible is its first letter
the letter from horrid goes inside the clue reference

parts.note: One Down is a clue earlier in this very puzzle, referred to in grid style

indicators.note: the end of horrid is its final letter

explanation.surface: Something terrible and horrid in an earlier clue has been softened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an earlier clue' is self-referential: 1 Down in this grid, spelt out in words as a crossword reference would be.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate something shocking is to soften its tone, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Spike Milligan's third one

indicators.note: the third letter of the name Milligan is wanted

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A third joke from the comedian Spike Milligan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like part of Milligan's name, the British Goon Show comedian, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike a drink is to secretly add alcohol or a drug, which is to lace it.

clue.text: Youth using phone catching every second of insane aria

parts.note: a lad is a youth

indicators.note: the phrase for using a phone holds the picked letters within it

parts.note: someone using the phone is on mobile

indicators.note: taking letters two, four and six of insane

explanation.surface: A young person on the phone catches every other bit of a mad aria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every second of' insane gives NAE; the Italian means 'woman is fickle', from Verdi's Rigoletto.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke's song from Verdi's Rigoletto is one of the best-known operatic arias.

clue.text: Performers very inspired by uplifting opera aria

parts.note: the cast are the performers in a show

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the letter goes inside
in a down entry, lifting up reads the word backwards

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: Performers are greatly inspired by an uplifting operatic aria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses AIDA to ADIA, which has V 'inspired by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma's prayer to the moon goddess in Bellini's opera is a celebrated soprano aria.

clue.text: Strong singer about to go down for high singer

parts.note: F is forte, the musical mark for loud and strong

indicators.note: the strong singer goes round the letters for going down

parts.note: an alto is a singer
the sun sets as it goes down

explanation.surface: A powerful singer about to be dropped in favour of a high-voiced one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer' appears twice: the first is wordplay, the second part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A male singer using falsetto produces notes above his natural range, so the word names a high voice.

clue.text: Head carrying knock, one's exposed

indicators.note: the head holds the word for knocking within it

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
to dis (or diss) is to knock or criticise

explanation.surface: A head injury leaves someone exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed, so is literally exposed.

clue.text: See 24
Where fox may be, one with a camel ultimately burying head in sand?

parts.note: a fox may be in its den
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the last letter of camel is taken

explanation.surface: A desert scene: a fox, a camel and someone hiding their head in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Burying your head in the sand is an idiom for refusing to face reality, the state of denial.

clue.text: Entering finale, all three starting in sensational style, unforgettable in opera aria

indicators.note: the assembled letters sit inside the opera's name

parts.note: Norma is Bellini's opera

indicators.note: the three initials go into the word for finale

parts.note: a finale is the end

indicators.note: the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A sensational, unforgettable finale to an opera aria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opera' is not the definition but Bellini's Norma; the aria itself is from Puccini's Turandot.
explanation.definitionFit: Calaf's tenor showpiece from Puccini's Turandot is perhaps the most famous of all arias.

clue.text: Wrong number held by user, or otherwise

indicators.note: the number is held within the rearranged letters
otherwise means in another way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is a number

explanation.surface: A user has the wrong number, or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges the letters of user and or, and 'held by' puts the number inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistaken or incorrect is a straightforward synonym for wrong.

clue.text: Silent, as sizeable frame in painting breaks head

indicators.note: the painting piece breaks into the headland word

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head

indicators.note: the frame letters go inside the painting word

parts.note: an oil is an oil painting

indicators.note: the frame of sizeable is its outside letters

explanation.surface: A large painting frame breaks over someone's head in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not the body part but a headland, a ness, as in Loch Ness's neighbours; 'as' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes no sound at all is silent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: An image awfully full of love, narcissism

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are filled with the love letter
awfully suggests the letters are badly arranged

parts.note: love is nil, O in tennis

explanation.surface: An awful picture full of self-love, a narcissist's portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges AN IMAGE into EGMANIA, 'full of' O after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissism is excessive self-love, an obsession with one's own ego.

clue.text: Sinner finally incarcerated, calling for heavy beating

indicators.note: locked up, so the letter is put inside

parts.note: dubbing is naming or calling

indicators.note: the final letter of Sinner

explanation.surface: A sinner jailed at last, with calls for a severe beating.
explanation.definitionFit: A drubbing is a thrashing, literally or as a heavy defeat.

clue.text: With vigour, cook cut bread

parts.note: brio is vigour or verve

indicators.note: cut means the word is shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: Briskly, a cook slices some bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a rich, sweet French bread made with eggs and butter.

clue.text: Pig flying at last, heading for terminal in airport

indicators.note: the last letter of flying
the terminal's initial goes inside the airport

parts.note: Luton is an airport near London

indicators.note: the head, first letter, of terminal

explanation.surface: Pigs might fly at last, landing at an airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig' and 'flying' recall the saying 'pigs might fly'; LUTON is a London airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is slang for a greedy eater, someone who overindulges.

clue.text: Nation today and for ever containing capital in Rome

indicators.note: the time words hold the capital letter

parts.note: now means today, at present

indicators.note: the capital, first letter, of Rome

parts.note: ay (aye) is an old word for always, for ever

explanation.surface: A nation, today and always, holding a capital in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for ever' as AY (aye) is an archaic, poetic use.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: See 1 across
See 1
When foaled, discard horse

parts.note: DOB is date of birth, when a foal was born
to bin is to throw away

explanation.surface: An old horse thrown out once born.
explanation.definitionFit: Dobbin is a traditional pet name for a workhorse or farm horse.

clue.text: See 12 across
Goddess of desire, Nephele

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A goddess of desire named Nephele, a cloud nymph of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene (Eirene) was the Greek goddess of peace.

clue.text: Aria where boy's a darling in mezzo-soprano, say?

definitions.text: Aria where boy's a darling in mezzo-soprano, say?

parts.words: Aria where boy's a darling in mezzo-soprano, say?
parts.note: Cherubino, the lovestruck page in Mozart's Marriage of Figaro, is a boy, a little cherub, sung by a mezzo-soprano in a trouser role

explanation.surface: An aria in which a boy, a darling, is voiced by a mezzo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'darling' points to cherub, inside the name Cherubino; the boy's part is sung by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubino's song of love's confusions in The Marriage of Figaro is a famous mezzo aria.

clue.text: Happy close to death, sang about it

indicators.note: the singing word goes round the letter

parts.note: trilled means sang with a warble

indicators.note: the close, last letter, of death

explanation.surface: Happy as death approaches, singing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilled means delighted, a strong synonym for happy.

clue.text: Man perhaps, one and only, lacking nothing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: lacking means the zero is taken out

parts.note: sole means only
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps the one and only, lacking anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Tongue in, well inside case of strawberries, beginning to eat

indicators.note: the beginning letter of eat

explanation.surface: Tongue goes into a punnet of strawberries as eating begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the body part, but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinhalese is the language of Sri Lanka's majority, so a tongue.
